texts: mixed: the meeting event and its Council agent are right, but the monthly-cycle atom comes from knowing how often full moons occur rather than from the words, so the parse asserts a period the sentence never states. Rewrite as "The Council meets every month, at the full moon." — the period is then stated outright and the full moon still fills the time slot.

good. both capitalized labels correctly stay common nouns with no name atom, sundown rides the time slot the way dawn or dusk does, and the Watch sits in an ordinary location slot on the meeting event.

mixed: a bare "sits at" clause mints no event and routes "at" onto the containment head, so the parse ends up saying the Council is located inside the table. Rewrite as "The Council meets at a long oak table." — a verb that reifies an event puts the table in an ordinary location slot instead, exactly as "meets at sundown in the Watch" already does in this section.
good. "oak" is a noun modifier, so the fused kind correctly carries only its head genus, and a bare copular with no reification trigger gives the flat property atom with no tense wrapper.

good. the name is one symbol with one Name atom, the fused council_speaker kind carries its genus, and Meren is typed by Member as an individual should be. The one thing no wording records is that the office is unique — "the speaker" comes out the same as "a speaker" — and there is no cleaner phrasing for it, so leave the sentence as it stands.

mixed: "item of business" is a category-restricting of-phrase that the instruction set does not legislate, so the restriction is improvised as a separate "of" link inside the rule's condition. Rewrite as "The speaker calls each business item." — an ordinary compound kind (genus "item") then carries the restriction, and the per-item rule keeps its "each" quantifier and stays fireable.
good. the compound kind carries its head genus with the modifier correctly left unexposed, the roles are right, and the decided order sits inside the default-to-Theme allowance.
